item.text:
**Configuration.** HTTPX defaults to 5 seconds each for `connect`, `read`, `write`, and `pool`. Set a client-wide default with `Client(timeout=...)` or `AsyncClient(timeout=...)`, and override it per request with `timeout=...`. A number applies to all four phases, `httpx.Timeout(...)` lets you configure them individually, and `None` disables timeouts. [httpx/_config.py](<work>/httpx-rules-official-codex/httpx/_config.py:72)

**Propagation.** `build_request()` stores the effective settings in `request.extensions["timeout"]` and preserves an explicitly supplied timeout extension. Sync and async `send()` fill in the client default if the extension is missing. [httpx/_client.py](<work>/httpx-rules-official-codex/httpx/_client.py:340)

**Enforcement.** The default sync and async transports forward the extension to `httpcore`, which enforces the limits when acquiring a pooled connection, establishing a connection, and waiting for individual reads or writes. These are phase-specific limits. HTTPX maps `httpcore` timeout exceptions to `ConnectTimeout`, `ReadTimeout`, `WriteTimeout`, and `PoolTimeout`. Custom transports are responsible for honoring the extension. [httpx/_transports/default.py](<work>/httpx-rules-official-codex/httpx/_transports/default.py:79) · [docs/advanced/extensions.md](<work>/httpx-rules-official-codex/docs/advanced/extensions.md:121)
